question.text: Which of the following is NOT an exception to the requirement that FPIs must transact only through registered stockbrokers?

answer.text: Sale of securities in response to a takeover offer under SAST Regulations, 2011
Transactions in Government securities as specified by RBI
Sale of securities in accordance with SEBI (Buy-back of Securities) Regulations, 2018
Purchase of shares through an initial public offering (IPO) directly from the company

explanation.text: The Logic: The broker-only rule has a defined list of exceptions including Government/RBI-specified securities, takeover offers under SAST, buybacks, disinvestment, corporate bonds, EBP-platform transactions and similar specified categories. A direct IPO purchase from the company is not in that list. The Trap: The three other options each map to an exception expressly carved out in the regulations; only the direct-from-company IPO route does not appear there. Note: Treat the answer as a literal match against the listed exceptions in the FPI regulations rather than as a general statement about how FPIs participate in primary issues.
